Planning on driving in Brantford’s downtown? Here’s an update of ongoing construction

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 0:55
Instaread

Those planning to attend Brantford's Remembrance Day service are advised to follow posted signage and allow extra travel time due to ongoing construction work.

By
Vincent Ball
November 9, 2026 at 12:18 p.m.
Last Updated: November 9, 2026 at 12:22 p.m.

The Remembrance Day service in Brantford will go ahead as planned despite ongoing construction in the downtown, city officials say.

The construction has impacted traffic flow in and around the downtown and those planning to attend the service are advised to follow posted signage and allow extra travel time.

Meanwhile, lane reductions remain in place this week on Dalhousie Street and Brant
Avenue. The Lorne Bridge remains reduced to a single eastbound lane with westbound lanes open. Colborne Street and Bridge Street closures remain in place

Detour routes are being monitored and adjusted as needed to support traffic flow, the city said in an update. The Veterans Memorial Parkway remains open without construction obstructions.

Local businesses directly affected by construction have been notified. Businesses will remain open during this time, including those located along Colborne Street east of Brant Avenue.

To learn more about the city’s road construction work visit
Brantford.ca/RoadClosures.
